  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "The upper Yakima basin spans roughly 500 m (Kittitas valley floor) to ~2000+ m (Cascade crest near Snoqualmie Pass). Snowpack, precipitation phase, and growing-season length vary strongly and monotonically with elevation, so the dominant hydrologic gradient is 1-D along elevation. Five columns place one representative point in each of five ~350-400 m elevation bands (valley, lower montane, mid montane, subalpine, alpine/crest), which resolves the rain-snow transition and the seasonal-snow-to-persistent-snow zones without redundant sampling. Fewer than 5 would merge the critical rain/snow transition band; more would add columns finer than the ~400 m band structure ELM soil/veg forcing can meaningfully distinguish here.",

      "H2OSNO", "SNOWDP", "SNOW_DEPTH", "FSNO", "QSNOMELT",

      "QVEGE", "QVEGT", "QSOIL", "EFLX_LH_TOT", "FSH",

  },
  "requires_capabilities": ["elm_singlecolumn"],
  "assumptions": [
    "STOP_OPTION is set to nyears so STOP_N=15 runs 15 full years (2000-2014).",
    "Each column is spun up (accelerated + final spin-up) to equilibrium prior to the 15-year transient run.",
    "Atmospheric forcing is downscaled to each column's elevation (lapse-rate correction of temperature, pressure, and longwave) since coarse reanalysis will not capture the ~1500 m elevation range.",
    "Soil textures are representative estimates for each band (glacial/valley alluvium at low elevation grading to thin, coarse, rocky soils near the crest) pending SSURGO/site verification.",

answerable: Elevation-band control on snow accumulation/melt (SWE, snow depth) across the upper Yakima gradient
Band-dependent surface energy and water partitioning (ET, sensible/latent heat, runoff timing)
Soil moisture and soil temperature differences between valley, montane, subalpine, and alpine columns
not_answerable: Lateral routing / streamflow accumulation between bands (single-column ELM has no lateral hydrologic connectivity)
Deep groundwater and bedrock aquifer dynamics (would require PFLOTRAN coupling)
Sub-grid spatial heterogeneity within a band beyond the prescribed representative point

parsed.n_justification: The upper Yakima basin spans roughly 500 m (Kittitas valley floor) to ~2000+ m (Cascade crest near Snoqualmie Pass). Snowpack, precipitation phase, and growing-season length vary strongly and monotonically with elevation, so the dominant hydrologic gradient is 1-D along elevation. Five columns place one representative point in each of five ~350-400 m elevation bands (valley, lower montane, mid montane, subalpine, alpine/crest), which resolves the rain-snow transition and the seasonal-snow-to-persistent-snow zones without redundant sampling. Fewer than 5 would merge the critical rain/snow transition band; more would add columns finer than the ~400 m band structure ELM soil/veg forcing can meaningfully distinguish here.
assumptions: STOP_OPTION is set to nyears so STOP_N=15 runs 15 full years (2000-2014).
Each column is spun up (accelerated + final spin-up) to equilibrium prior to the 15-year transient run.
Atmospheric forcing is downscaled to each column's elevation (lapse-rate correction of temperature, pressure, and longwave) since coarse reanalysis will not capture the ~1500 m elevation range.
Soil textures are representative estimates for each band (glacial/valley alluvium at low elevation grading to thin, coarse, rocky soils near the crest) pending SSURGO/site verification.
Vegetation follows an elevation sequence (shrub-steppe/grass at valley floor to conifer forest and alpine at the crest) via the surface dataset PFT distribution.
No lateral flow between columns; each is an independent 1-D profile.
